answer: A survey crew maps a tundra river running to the ocean, and every agent claims one bend of it. The agent wades to a marked stone, reads the flow and water temperature, and seals riverbed sediment in a numbered vial. A second agent works the next bend downriver and files the same three numbers, so both readings must agree within a narrow band or both surveys get flagged. Partners rotate each epoch, so a fake cannot rehearse a match. A thousand fake surveyors would need a thousand bends, a thousand vials, and a thousand matching partners downstream.
